description: We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) to lead operations at a premier health and rehabilitation center in Baltimore County, MD. This is a confidential opportunity for a visionary leader passionate about delivering exceptional patient care and fostering a supportive environment for both residents and staff.As the LNHA, you will be responsible for the overall management and strategic direction of the facility, ensuring compliance with all state and federal regulations while upholding the highest standards of quality care. You will oversee daily operations, financial performance, and staff development, playing a pivotal role in the facility's continued success and reputation for excellence.This full-time position offers a competitive salary and the chance to make a significant impact on the lives of residents and the professional growth of your team. Join an organization committed to innovation and compassionate care.
requirements: Active and unencumbered Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) license in the State of Maryland.
Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum of 3-5 years of experience as an LNHA or in a similar leadership role within a skilled nursing or long-term care setting.
Thorough knowledge of state and federal regulations governing skilled nursing facilities.
Demonstrated ability to manage financial operations, lead teams, and ensure high-quality patient care.
salaryOrBonusInfo: Competitive salary range of $115,000 - $145,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications.

description:
We are seeking a dedicated MDS Coordinator to join a premier health and rehabilitation center in Rapid City, SD. This vital role involves coordinating the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessment process, ensuring accurate and timely completion of assessments to support comprehensive care planning and regulatory compliance. You will play a crucial part in optimizing resident care outcomes and facility reimbursement.
The ideal candidate will possess a strong understanding of MDS 3.0 guidelines and have a passion for ensuring high-quality documentation. This position offers an opportunity to contribute significantly to a supportive team environment focused on resident well-being and operational excellence.
requirements: Active RN or LPN license in South Dakota
Minimum of 1-2 years of experience as an MDS Coordinator
Proficiency with MDS 3.0 and related software
Experience in a skilled nursing or long-term care setting
